items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: I was lucky to play in his expanded group that did tours. We did tours of the East Coast and Midwest.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about Chuck Mangione. So I’m moving ahead a little bit and you’re at Eastman and Chuck was well known locally. Was he doing like an adjunct at Eastman at that time?

Yeah he was. When I went Rayburn Wright was also the first year that Ray Wright came, he came from Radio City Music Hall where he was the music director of that. He worked his way up through the arranging ranks and ended up as the head musical guy at Radio City. And he had been teaching some courses in the summer at Eastman, some arranging courses, called “The Arranger’s Workshop.” And he was then, thought it was time for him to move from the city and have a little less hectic life — not less busy though because…

ensemble concerts and there’d be 3,000 people there. The Eastman Theater would be packed. And they weren’t charging anything. Still, to get 3,000 people for a school show, you know, was pretty impressive. And so that happened and Chuck continued to gain popularity and because of that he started doing bigger records and doing some tours and I was lucky to play in his expanded group that did tours. We did tours of the East Coast and Midwest. He had me come to California once to do a recording there in Herb…
